subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: The language of trends: increase, decrease and describing a table / Road rage: Listening 4.3.2, advice and role play
outcomes: Use verbs, nouns and adverbs to describe trends
Describe numbers in a table with trend language
Give advice to avoid road rage

tf.s: A trend is the way a situation changes over a period of time.
tf.why: Yes, trends show change over time.
Correct, they all show a fall.

tf.s: We say 'an increase in' the number of cars.
tf.why: Yes, the noun 'increase' is followed by 'in'.
The adverb is 'steadily': y changes to i.

tf.s: Tailgating means driving too close to the car in front.
tf.why: Right, and it makes drivers nervous.
Yes, they show large, fast changes.

tf.s: When another driver makes you angry, the best advice is to stay calm.
When someone cuts in, the other driver feels relaxed.
tf.why: Driver 4 had to brake sharply and felt scared.

boxes.q: What did Driver 4 do when someone cut in?
boxes.why: He had to brake and feared an accident.

boxes.q: How does tailgating make a driver feel?

o: showing which way you will turn
boxes.why: Indicators tell others where you are going.

boxes.q: Which is a polite thing a driver could say?
o: Sorry, I didn't see you – go ahead.

boxes.q: Which adjective describes a small change?

o: anger of drivers on the road
boxes.why: Road rage is angry, aggressive driving.

hunt.q: Lights that show you will turn
A change over a period of time

mcq.q: Which list contains only verbs for going up?
mcq.why: These four all show an upward trend.

mcq.q: Why is flashing lights at other drivers rude?
o: It is aggressive and tries to push other drivers out of the way
It shows you will turn left
It is a way to say thank you
mcq.why: Flashing lights can frighten other drivers.

mcq.q: Why is turning without signals a problem?
o: Other drivers don't know if you will go left or right
It is the law to not signal
mcq.why: Signals help others understand your plan.

mcq.q: Which adjective describes a slow, regular change?
mcq.why: A gradual change happens little by little.

mcq.q: The number of vehicles went up a lot. Which sentence fits?
o: There was a sharp increase in the number of vehicles.
There was a slight decrease in the number of vehicles.
The number of vehicles fell sharply.
There was a sharp increase on vehicles.
mcq.why: A big rise is a sharp increase in…

mcq.q: Accidents went from 500 to 490 in one year. How can you describe this?
o: There was a slight drop in accidents.
There was a dramatic rise in accidents.
mcq.why: A fall of 10 out of 500 is small.

mcq.q: A driver is tailgating you and you feel nervous. What is the best advice?
o: Stay calm and let the other driver pass
Brake suddenly to teach him a lesson
mcq.why: Letting him pass keeps you safe.

mcq.q: What is the difference between 'rise' and 'drop'?
o: 'Rise' means go up; 'drop' means go down
'Rise' means go down; 'drop' means go up
The other driver must brake sharply and an accident may happen

mcq.q: Why does staying calm help to avoid road rage?
o: Calm drivers make safer decisions and do not make things worse
It means you never need to stop
mcq.why: Keeping cool stops problems from growing.
